newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen signs pact to buy G&L.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen signs pact to buy G&L.

text.p: Thyssen AG said on Thursday it had signed a definitive agreement to acquire U.S. machine tools maker Giddings & Lewis for $21 a share in cash.
The acquisition is worth about $675 million, based on Giddings & Lewis's 32.1 million outstanding shares, a Thyssen spokeswoman said.
The tender offer will be made over the next five days, and G&L shareholders will have 20 days to accept it, she said.
The Thyssen offer of $21 a share overtakes a rival $19 a share offer made in late April by Harnischfeger Industries Inc, which G&L management rejected as inadequate.
Thyssen signs pact to buy G&L
The statement quoted Thyssen chairman Dieter Vogel as saying, "Giddings & Lewis is the ideal fit with Thyssen to enhance our core production systems business."

G&L chief executive officer Marvin Isles said, "Our board of directors unanimously concluded that this transaction with Thyssen is in the best interests of all Giddings & Lewis' constituencies. At $21 per share in cash, Gidding & Lewis shareholders will receive exceptional value."
The statement said G&L would pay Thyssen a fee of $20 million plus $3 million in expenses if under certain circumstances the agreement were terminated by G&L for another acquisition transaction.
The merger is subject to antitrust reveiew in the U.S., Germany and other countries.
